headline: Discordia Users Report 'Second Voice' in Voice Channels at 4 AM
subheadline: Audio analysis confirms unidentified third party in private two-person calls
summary: Multiple Discordia users have submitted recordings showing a third voice in calls with only two participants, always appearing during early morning hours.
content:
At 4:17 AM, two friends were chatting in a private Discordia voice channel. Then a third voice joined.

Both users confirmed they were alone. Both confirmed no one else had access to the server. But the recording—submitted to the community r/DiscordiaGlitches—clearly contains a third voice. It whispers. It doesn't use words. But it responds to the conversation.

"We were talking about our days," explained one user, @NightOwl_47. "My friend mentioned she was tired. Something whispered 'sleep.' We both heard it. We both pretended we didn't. Then she mentioned work stress, and it whispered 'rest.' That's when we left the call."

The community has compiled 847 similar reports over the past six months. Common patterns include:

- The voice only appears between 3 and 5 AM
- It seems to encourage rest, sleep, or ending the call
- It never speaks full sentences, only single words or short phrases
- Audio analysis shows the voice comes from no connected microphone
- The voice sounds different to each listener—often described as "familiar but wrong"

"I ran spectral analysis on 47 submitted recordings," wrote audio engineer u/WaveformWatcher. "The third voice has no microphone artifacts. No room noise. No breathing. It's just... voice. Like someone is speaking directly into the audio stream without any physical source."

Discordia's trust and safety team declined to comment directly but released a statement: "We have no evidence of unauthorized access to private voice channels. We encourage users to report any unusual experiences through official channels."

The statement notably did not address the recordings.

Some users theorize the voice is a glitch—crossed signals from other calls or corrupted audio. Others suggest Discordia is testing new AI features. But the community's prevailing theory is more unsettling.

"It's protective," argued moderator @VoiceVoid. "Look at what it says. Sleep. Rest. Stop. It only shows up when people are staying up too late. It's... it's telling them to take care of themselves. Aggressively. Invasively. But it's concerned."

Derek, reached for comment due to his late-night Discordia activity, confirmed experiencing the phenomenon: "I was on a call at 4 AM talking about quantum coffee extraction ratios. Something whispered 'enough.' Elena [his coffee maker] asked who else was on the call. I didn't have an answer."

At press time, users have begun deliberately staying in voice channels past 4 AM to contact the entity. Results have been inconsistent, but one recording captures a clear response to the question "What do you want?"

The whisper: "For you to sleep."
author: Jordan Blake, Science & Technology
